proposal: The Mandate says a conservative administration should include a citizenship question in the decennial census, relying on the Supreme Court's 2019 holding that the Commerce Secretary has broad authority to add one. It also recommends reviewing the planned race and ethnicity question changes and all decennial and American Community Survey questions, auditing 2030 census planning and budgets, and abolishing the Census Bureau's National Advisory Committee and other non-statutory advisory committees. Topics are due to Congress by April 1, 2027 and questions by April 1, 2028.
remaining: Final decision on whether the 2030 census form carries a citizenship or legal-status question; topics are due to Congress by 2027-04-01 and the questions by 2028-04-01.
OMB decision on the citizenship item in the 2026 test (not confirmed) and publication of test results.
Final rule on residence criteria and demographic questions after the comment period closes on 2026-11-02.

status_summary: The Census Bureau's advisory committees (including the National Advisory Committee) are no longer operating; its website says as of its August 2026 revision that it has no advisory committees, after meetings were cancelled in March 2025. A Federal Register notice of 2026-02-03 sought OMB approval for a 2026 operational test, and NPR reported the filing indicated respondents may be asked about citizenship (OMB approval of that item was not confirmed). On 2026-09-10 the Bureau proposed rules that would count only U.S. citizens and lawful permanent residents toward apportionment (other foreign nationals, including people in the country illegally and those with temporary or indefinite status, would not be counted), invite comment on adding a legal-status question to the short form, and bar race, ethnicity and sexual-orientation questions from the enumeration form; the comment period now runs to 2026-11-02. The proposal does not itself add a citizenship question, and no 2030 questions have been finalized.

timeline.event: The Census Bureau publishes Federal Register notices (dated 2025-03-10 through 2025-03-13) cancelling meetings of the Census Scientific Advisory Committee, the 2030 Census Advisory Committee and the National Advisory Committee. The Bureau later states it has no advisory committees.

NPR reports that Commerce official George Cook is named acting Census director and that President Trump has called for a new census excluding residents without legal status; legal experts quoted say a new count before 2030 would need congressional authorization and funding.
Census Bureau submits its information collection for the 2026 Operational Test in Support of the 2030 Census to OMB (about 154,600 respondents; internet self-response and in-field enumeration).

NPR reports the filing says test participants may be asked about U.S. citizenship status, pending OMB approval; the test runs April to September 2026 in Huntsville, Alabama and Spartanburg, South Carolina, and is based on the American Community Survey form.

Proposed rule 'Decennial Census of the Population of Americans' (91 FR 57524) would add 15 CFR parts 60 and 70: residence criteria counting only U.S. citizens and lawful permanent residents toward apportionment, a request for comment on a short-form legal-status question, and limits on demographic questions (sex, date of birth and household relationships allowed; race, ethnicity and sexual orientation barred).
The Census Bureau extends the comment period on the proposed rule from 2026-10-13 to 2026-11-02.

title: Add a citizenship question to the census and reshape Census Bureau operations
uncertainties: Could not confirm whether OMB approved the citizenship item in the 2026 test, or the date and exact wording of the President's August 2025 call for a new census (cited only through NPR's later reporting). Formal termination of the National Advisory Committee is inferred from the Bureau's page and March 2025 meeting cancellations; no termination notice was found. Litigation by states on apportionment was not researched beyond what the proposed rule and NPR describe. The Federal Register full-text search on 'citizenship question' returned no Census documents. The shared search budget ran out before news searches on these points.
